documents.author: patient
documents.body: I think I'm overdue for a physical, haven't had one since 2022 with the babies. Do you have anything on a Tuesday after 3? I'm off Tuesdays in March.

documents.title: Scheduled

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical — 33F

Interval: two emergency cesareans for uterine rupture (9/2023, 9/2024), both repaired at the regional hospital. Recovered from the last one; back at work full time since January. Four kids at home. No concerns today other than feeling she never has time to exercise.

Meds: ferrous sulfate 325 TID, PNV with iron daily, calcium carbonate 600 BID. Allergy: sulfa.
Never smoker, no alcohol.

ROS negative.

Exam: wt 88.9 kg, BMI 34.9. Vitals reviewed.
General: well, NAD.
HEENT: normal. Neck: no thyroid enlargement, no nodes.
Heart: regular rhythm, no murmur. Lungs: clear.
Abd: soft, nontender, healed transverse scar.
Ext: no edema. Skin: no concerning lesions.
PHQ-2: 0.

A/P
- Preventive: CBC, iron, CMP, lipids, A1c. Pap/HPV up to date (negative 10/2022), next 2027. Immunizations current — flu and COVID last fall.
- Iron deficiency anemia: recheck on TID iron.
- Obesity: BMI 34.9. Small goals — walking with the stroller on days off.
RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Gladys — hemoglobin 11.5 and ferritin 15, both much better than October. Cholesterol, A1c, kidney and liver numbers are all normal. Same plan: keep the iron going.

documents.body: eRx renewal requests: ferrous sulfate 325 mg TID #90 x 5; calcium carbonate 1500 mg BID #60 x 11. Pended — PCP approved both.

documents.title: Positive pregnancy test
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt calling with positive home test, LMP 7/23/25. No bleeding, no pain. Knows she needs MFM again right away, asked us to send the referral the same as last time. Appt with PCP Thurs 9/4. Reviewed: pain, bleeding, or popping sensation at any point = 911/L&D.

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 33F, LMP 7/23/25, ~6 wks. Two prior uterine ruptures at term with emergency cesarean and repair (9/2023, 9/2024), plus two earlier cesareans. Asymptomatic. On PNV, iron TID, calcium.

O: Wt 89.6. Vitals reviewed. Well appearing. Abd soft, nontender, scar well healed.
Urine hCG positive.

A/P:
1. Pregnancy after two uterine ruptures — very high risk. Referral to MFM today, same group as 2024; RN calling to expedite. Precautions reviewed in detail.
2. Iron deficiency anemia — CBC today, continue iron and PNV.
3. We will follow along with MFM.

documents.title: Blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hemoglobin 12.1, a little better than March. MFM has the referral and has you down for the end of the month.

documents.title: Maternal-fetal medicine consultation
documents.author: maternal-fetal medicine
documents.body:
Maternal-Fetal Medicine, Regional Hospital
Date of visit: 09/30/2025
Re: Gladys Perez, DOB 01/15/1992

Thank you for referring Ms. Perez, now G5P4 at 9 weeks 6 days by LMP, with a single viable intrauterine pregnancy on today's scan. She is well known to our service: uterine rupture at term in September 2023 and again in September 2024, each managed with emergency cesarean and repair, after two earlier low transverse cesareans.
Other history: iron deficiency anemia on oral iron, obesity.
Allergies: sulfa drugs.
Current medications: prenatal vitamin with iron; ferrous sulfate 325 mg TID; calcium carbonate 600 mg BID.

We reviewed the risks of a third rupture openly with the patient and her husband. She wishes to continue the pregnancy. Plan: visits every 2-4 weeks, serial ultrasound, low threshold for admission, and planned cesarean before labor; we also discussed definitive surgical options at delivery and will revisit these as the pregnancy progresses.

Maternal-Fetal Medicine Attending

events.reason: Abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding at 37 weeks

conditions.label: Abnormality in fetal heart rate and rhythm complicating labor and delivery
Supervision of high risk pregnancy, unspecified, unspecified trimester
Acquired absence of uterus and cervix
conditions.note: Total abdominal hysterectomy at cesarean, ovaries conserved

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every 6 hours as needed for pain

reports.text: Specimen: uterus and cervix, hysterectomy. Gross: gravid-sized uterus with attached cervix, opened. Microscopic: full-thickness disruption of the myometrium with associated hemorrhage, consistent with rupture. Endometrium with decidual change. Cervix with no significant pathologic abnormality. No other abnormality identified.
reports.conclusion: Uterus with full-thickness myometrial disruption consistent with rupture; benign cervix.

documents.title: ED Provider Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Arrival 04/08/2026 21:15

CC: abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, pregnant 37 wks

HPI: 34 yo G5P4 at 37w0d, MFM patient, with uterine rupture at term in September 2023 and again in September 2024. Tonight sudden severe abdominal pain, constant, going through to her back, with vaginal bleeding. Says it feels like the last two times.

PMH: IDA, obesity, uterine rupture x2. PSH: cesarean x4.
Meds: PNV with iron, ferrous sulfate 325 TID, calcium carbonate 600 BID.
Allergies: sulfa drugs.

VS: BP 100/60, HR 110.
Exam: in obvious distress. Fundus tender; contour of the abdomen irregular on palpation.
FHR: late decelerations.
Labs: Hgb 9.8, Hct 29, plt 210, WBC 12.0.

Imp: recurrent uterine rupture. OB/MFM and anesthesia at bedside within minutes; to OR.
Dispo: OR, then surgical ICU.

documents.title: Operative Report — cesarean hysterectomy
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Date: 04/08/2026
Pre-op: suspected third uterine rupture, 37 weeks, fetal heart rate decelerations.
Post-op: uterine rupture, third occurrence.
Procedure: emergency laparotomy, cesarean delivery, total abdominal hysterectomy with conservation of both ovaries.
Anesthesia: general endotracheal.
Allergies: sulfa drugs.

Findings: uterine rupture confirmed. Liveborn infant delivered and handed off to neonatology (NICU). Given a third rupture of a previously repaired uterus, hysterectomy was performed as discussed antenatally. Ovaries normal and preserved.
Transfusion: 2 units packed red blood cells intraoperatively.
Specimen: uterus and cervix to pathology.
Extubated in the OR. Transferred to the surgical ICU in stable condition.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Admitted 04/08/2026 — Discharged 04/13/2026
Units: ED, OR, surgical ICU (04/08-04/10), postpartum floor.

Diagnoses: third uterine rupture during labor at 37 weeks; fetal heart rate abnormality; anemia of pregnancy; status post emergency cesarean delivery and total abdominal hysterectomy with ovarian conservation; iron deficiency anemia; obesity.

Course: arrived with BP 100/60, HR 110 and Hgb 9.8. Emergency cesarean hysterectomy; 2 units PRBC in the OR. Two nights in the SICU for monitoring, then the postpartum unit. Hgb nadir 8.9 on POD1, 9.3 on POD4. Pathology: uterus with full-thickness myometrial disruption consistent with rupture; benign cervix. Infant cared for in the NICU.

Allergies: sulfa drugs.
Discharge medications: prenatal vitamin with iron daily; ferrous sulfate 325 mg three times daily; calcium carbonate 600 mg twice daily; ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours as needed.

Follow-up: gynecology postoperative visit 6 weeks; primary care 1 week (anemia, transition of care).

documents.title: Transitional care call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: TCM call day after discharge. Pt home, husband off work this week. Pain controlled with ibuprofen. Incision intact per pt, no drainage, no fever. Minimal spotting. Tired. Baby in NICU. Taking iron TID. Hospital records requested, expected this week. Seeing PCP Tues 4/21.

conditions.label: Abnormality in fetal heart rate and rhythm complicating labor and delivery

documents.title: Post-Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM — third uterine rupture, cesarean hysterectomy

Regional hospital 4/8-4/13: at 37 wks sudden pain to the back with bleeding; BP 100/60, HR 110, Hgb 9.8. Emergency cesarean with total abdominal hysterectomy, ovaries kept. 2 u PRBC. SICU 2 nights. Hgb 8.9 nadir, 9.3 at discharge. Path: rupture, benign cervix. Records reviewed in full.

S: 13 days out. Pain much better, ibuprofen once a day. No fever, incision fine, minimal spotting. Baby came home Friday. Emotionally: "relieved it's over and sad there won't be more." Sleeping when she can. Taking ferrous sulfate TID, PNV, calcium.

O: Wt 91.3. Vitals reviewed. Tired but comfortable, mildly pale.
Heart: regular, no murmur. Lungs: clear.
Abd: transverse incision healing well, no erythema, no drainage; appropriately tender. No calf tenderness or edema.
PHQ-9: 3.

A/P:
1. S/p cesarean hysterectomy for recurrent uterine rupture — recovering well. Uterus and cervix removed; problem list updated. No further cervical cancer screening needed (benign indication, cervix removed). Gyn post-op visit late May.
2. Iron deficiency anemia, post-hemorrhage/transfusion — CBC and iron today. Continue ferrous sulfate TID.
3. Mood — PHQ-9 3, good support. Will keep asking.
RTC 3 months for anemia.

documents.title: Blood count after surgery
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hemoglobin is 10.0, up from 9.3 when you left the hospital. Ferritin is 9, so your iron stores are low again. Keep taking the iron three times a day. Now that you won't have periods or pregnancies, these numbers should climb steadily. Recheck in July.

documents.title: RE: Blood count after surgery
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you for everything. Will do.

documents.title: Gynecology postoperative letter
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Obstetrics & Gynecology, Regional Hospital
Postoperative visit 05/20/2026
Re: Gladys Perez, DOB 01/15/1992

Dear Doctor,

Ms. Perez was seen six weeks after emergency cesarean delivery and total abdominal hysterectomy (ovaries conserved) on 04/08/2026 for a third uterine rupture. She is recovering well. Incision is fully healed. Vaginal cuff examination normal. Pathology was reviewed with her: rupture of the uterus, benign cervix.

Allergies: sulfa drugs.

She may resume all usual activity, including work. As the cervix was removed for a benign indication, no further cervical screening is needed. No routine gynecologic follow-up is required; we are happy to see her for any new concern.

Kind regards,
Obstetrics & Gynecology

S: 3 months after cesarean hysterectomy. Back at work since mid-June, energy improving week by week. Gyn released her in May. Still taking ferrous sulfate TID, PNV, calcium. Baby and the other kids well.

O: Wt 88.7. Vitals reviewed. Looks well, color better than April.
Heart regular, lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender, scar healed.
PHQ-2: 0.

1. Iron deficiency anemia — CBC and iron today, expect improvement. Same iron regimen.
2. Obesity — weight back down near her baseline. Will keep working on it at the physical.
3. S/p hysterectomy — no further gyn follow-up or Pap needed.
Physical in October.

documents.title: Blood count

documents.body: Nice improvement: hemoglobin 12.1, back in the normal range (from 10.0 in April), and ferritin 19. Keep the iron going and we'll recheck at your physical in October.
